data.name: Jamiaah
data.gender_notes: Jamiaah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic tradition, the name Jamiaah symbolizes a large gathering or assembly of people. It is derived from the Arabic root 'jama'a' which means 'to gather' or 'to assemble'. This name is often given to girls in the hope that they will bring people together and foster unity and solidarity. The name Jamiaah carries the meaning “Gathering, crowd” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Jamiaah usually hope their child will grow to embody gathering, crowd and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of unity and togetherness in the Muslim community.
data.etymology: Jamiaah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gathering, crowd.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jamiaah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_urdu.name: جامعہ
in_urdu.meaning: جامعہ کا مطلب ہے اکٹھا کرنا،รวม کرنا

in_hindi.name: जामिया

This name holds significant importance in Islamic tradition, symbolizing unity and the coming together of people or things. It reflects the values of togetherness and collective growth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jamiaah reflects the importance of community and camaraderie in Islamic culture. It implies that the individual is just a tiny piece of a larger whole, and that the strength and unity of this collective gathering is essential to society. Additionally, it suggests the bringing together of minds and hearts through shared knowledge, traditions, and goals.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jamiaah holds spiritual significance as well, as it can be seen as a reminder of the unity of all believers in the faith of Islam. All Muslims worldwide are part of this global Jamiaah or collective community. Additionally, the name symbolizes the gathering of seekers of knowledge, as in the famous Islamic university Al-Jamia al-Islamia or Al-Azhar University. This pursuit of knowledge is considered a key aspect of spiritual growth and development in Islam.
